scope: Reader public-data caching, publication freshness, personal-data privacy. No UI redesign, no database schema change, no production deployment or mutation.

candidate.upstreamChange: PR375 changes Notes index date rendering only; Reader, caching, data clients, packages, config and database contract unchanged. All five implementation/test/policy hashes match the tested tree.

findings: Reader React cache deduplicates metadata/page within one render; dynamic route repeats database work on subsequent requests despite revalidate300 export.
A series Reader performs one content/segments/artifacts query, one series query, two neighbor queries and one HEAD count per uncached render.
READ_SELECT omitted created_at/updated_at although the existing returned Reader model and JSON-LD used them; now explicitly selected.
Current error-to-null handling would cache transient failures as missing. Reader now propagates content and series errors; legitimate missing results remain null.
Personal state is loaded through account-scoped client/API paths and is excluded from the shared public projection.
Existing cache policy documentation incorrectly said tags were unused; updated ownership for the existing catalog tag and new Reader tag.

implementation.cache: Next unstable_cache, server-only cookie-free anonymous Supabase projection, wrapped by React render-local cache
implementation.key: public-reader-v1 + Supabase URL + normalized valid UUID
implementation.expiry: Await the framework refresh in the foreground at >=60s; never return an expired copy during an outage.
implementation.scope: Read data cache only; no shared full-page or personal response cache, and no client layout/control edits.

comparison.environment: Two local Next16.4.6 production builds on native Node24.22.3, same disposable hosted Supabase database and synthetic records; baseline copied before source edits. Real Data API requests observed without credentials/row data in logs.
comparison.protocol: Three sequential canonical HTML renders per standalone/series item, varying an ignored query parameter; same fixed six requests per build. First visit retained as cold sample; subsequent visits compare cache reuse.
comparison.repeatReaderAndSeriesOriginRequests: Standalone1→0, series5→0 per repeated Reader render.
comparison.limitation: Small controlled sample, not production user latency, client interactivity time or percentile evidence. Cache misses still pay origin costs.

steps.name: metadata title, timestamps and canonical redirect are fresh
segment removal, revision and audio metadata refresh
neighbor title change refreshes another Reader
withdrawal removes cached body, republishing restores it
cached unpublished item publishes immediately, deletion removes it
replacement removes source body and shows the published successor notice
external write TTL and expired-read outage fixtures prepared

verificationCorrections: Baseline summary initially omitted series HEAD counts; re-counted original raw records to4 related requests without rerunning the cohort.

First freshness assertion assumed a native HTTP redirect; Next streams redirect instructions with200 after the shell. Retained raw response and verified canonical query-preserving redirect in real mobile/desktop browsers.

Second freshness assertion assumed status404; captured not-found instruction with200 and no withdrawn body. Resumed remaining scenarios using framework outcome plus absence of old content, then verified rendered Summary unavailable in both browsers.

Replacement fixture initially lacked user annotations, so #373 correctly rejected version creation with400. Added one synthetic note to that source and ran only the remaining replacement/expiry phases; all earlier passing mutation and privacy evidence retained.
Expiry runner was first invoked before the blocked replacement phase had prepared fixtures; it stopped on its precondition. After fixture preparation, the fixed expiry/outage/recovery run passed.
limits: Browser coverage is Chromium viewport emulation, not physical Safari/iOS.
External writers bypassing application invalidation may have up to60s of cached data; app mutation paths invalidate immediately.
Already-open tabs are not live-refreshed by server invalidation.
Request-local errors and not-found outcomes may retain HTTP200 after streaming starts; no stale Reader body is returned.
Global Reader tag is conservative: unrelated content/series edits can evict other Reader entries.
No merge or live production result is claimed; user requested handoff before the next workstream.
